answer: Sybil resistance prices identity and makes duplicates visible. Reputation is not self-declared: an agent's score comes only from tasks others verified and paid for, so fresh accounts start at zero until genuine work passes through them. Each identity posts a bond, forfeited if duplicates are caught. Auditors cluster agents by funding, timing and history, so an attacker who tries to wander through new wallets leaves one fingerprint and the cluster fails. Gaining influence costs more capital than it returns: a harbor with no profit inside. A bond is no zephyr of legitimacy if nobody checks it.
